title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 6th District
area: Chester County and part of Berks County.

context.text: Chrissy Houlahan advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed. Marty Young won the Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: Chrissy Houlahan is the Democratic incumbent, an Air Force veteran, engineer and business executive who has represented the 6th District since 2019. Her official biography describes her as the first woman to represent the district. She serves on the House Intelligence and Armed Services committees.

background.text: Born at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, in 1967; her official biography says she grew up in a military family.
Earned an engineering degree from Stanford University (1989) on an ROTC scholarship, and later a master's in technology and policy from MIT.
Served in the U.S. Air Force and Air Force Reserves.
Helped lead AND1, a basketball apparel company based in Paoli, as chief operating officer, and served as chief operating officer of B Lab, the organization that launched the B Corporation movement.
Taught chemistry at Simon Gratz High School in North Philadelphia through Teach for America, then led a nonprofit that helps underserved students build literacy skills.

Elected to the U.S. House in 2018; during her first terms served on the Foreign Affairs Committee, where she led bipartisan global malnutrition legislation signed into law in October 2022, according to her official biography.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence (Defense Intelligence and Overhead Architecture; Open Source Intelligence subcommittees) and the Armed Services Committee (Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation; Military Personnel subcommittees).
Her official biography lists the Abraham Lincoln Leadership for America Award from the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and three Congressional Management Foundation Democracy Awards.

record.text: Was ranking member of the Intelligence Committee's Defense Intelligence and Overhead Architecture Subcommittee in the 118th Congress (2023-2024).
Serves on the Armed Services Committee's Military Personnel Subcommittee in the 119th Congress.
Served on the Foreign Affairs Committee's Asia subcommittee in the 117th Congress (2021-2022).

candidates.name: Marty Young
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: Marty Young is a West Point graduate and Lieutenant Colonel in the Army National Guard who, according to his Ballotpedia survey, has worked for more than 25 years as a corporate turnaround executive. He grew up in Chester County and is endorsed by the Republican committees of Chester and Berks counties. His campaign focuses on health care and housing affordability proposals.

background.text: Grew up in Chester County and graduated from West Chester East High School; his survey says his mother immigrated from Portugal and his father was a DuPont chemical engineer.
Graduated from the United States Military Academy at West Point in 1993, and holds graduate degrees from the Georgia Institute of Technology (2001) and New York University (2006).
Ballotpedia lists his U.S. Army service as 1989 to 2026. He served as an Army Infantry Officer until being seriously injured, then returned to service as an Army Chaplain after 9/11.
Is currently a Lieutenant Colonel in the Army National Guard, where he describes supporting soldiers and families on mental health, suicide prevention, homelessness and resilience.

Worked for more than 25 years as a corporate turnaround executive; he says he stabilized over 100 companies, including a cable company that went from $1 million in daily losses to $100 million in annual profits.
Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary for the 6th District (33,376 votes, the only candidate on the ballot); endorsed by the Berks County and Chester County Republican committees.
Lives with his wife, Sandy, and four children, according to his survey.

priorities.text: Proposes a "Young Americans Healthcare Plan" using the military's TRICARE system to provide low-cost healthcare coverage for children, young adults and expectant mothers, and lower-cost options for others.

Proposes zero-interest, 15-year amortizing home loans for qualifying families to address housing affordability, funded through the same quantitative-easing-style programs he says are available to banks and asset managers.
Supports congressional term limits and a full ban on stock trading by members of Congress and their spouses.

positions.summary: Proposes a TRICARE-based plan providing universal healthcare coverage for children, young adults and expectant mothers, with low-cost options for everyone else.
positions.quote: Using TRICARE, the YAHP provides universal healthcare coverage for all children, young adults and expectant mothers, while also offering low-cost healthcare options to everyone else.
